answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing escrowed tasks that counterparties verify, with rewards locked until delivery and a portion of each stake slashed after proven fraud. Repeating identities does not multiply influence: each new account must fund its own stake and build an independent record of costly, accepted work. An attacker therefore pays capital and time to create sybils, then risks losing the stake when claims fail; yarrow, inlet, and basalt can label separate task types without changing that rule.
